title: DisagreePathVLM: A Disagreement-Aware Histopathology Classification and Vision-Language Reasoning Framework for Transparent Pathology Assessment
content: Histopathology image classification systems often achieve and attain high accuracy results and good predictive performance. But the model’s provide limited support for understanding model uncertainty and diagnostic disagreement. In this research we propose a DisagreePathVLM, a disagreement-aware pathology framework which integrates CNN as classifier, Grad-CAM to obtain the visual evidence and VLM (vision-language model) for final interpretation. We trained a ResNet50 classifier on LC25000 histopathology images and evaluated them on unseen samples. Grad-CAM is used to identify diagnostically relevant regions, which were subsequently analyzed by a VLM. Agreement analysis revealed that many samples received consistent predictions from both models, whereas disagreement cases showed substantially higher error rates and lower confidence stability. The findings suggest that model disagreement can serve as a practical indicator of diagnostic uncertainty and may support the development of more transparent and trustworthy AI-assisted pathology systems.
